page: Microsoft Azure D192ds_v6 is a high-scale general purpose virtual machine from the Ddsv6 series, powered by the Intel Xeon 8573C processor on the x86_64 architecture. The server configuration provides 192 vCPUs derived from 96 dedicated physical cores running at up to 4.2 GHz with 260 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 768 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and integrates 11,339 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Hardware extensions include AVX-512, Intel AMX for matrix operations, and hardware cryptography instructions, running under Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier parallel throughput across compute-heavy, memory-intensive, and caching workloads. The instance achieves top 10% ratings in stress-ng multi-core tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core execution, and software compilation via Clang. Database operations and memory access metrics also place in the top decile, demonstrated by 211.88 million Redis SET operations per second and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth exceeding 511 GB/s. In contrast, per-thread metrics such as single-core stress-ng tests and LLM text generation fall into the middle-to-strong tiers, highlighting that peak performance relies on parallel execution rather than single-threaded clock saturation.

Resource density justifies the deployment of this large footprint for centralized consolidation. The combination of massive parallel core capacity, 768 GB RAM, and over 11 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage reduces inter-node networking overhead typical of distributed setups. It is specifically suited for high-concurrency databases, in-memory caching platforms like Redis, enterprise CI/CD compilation pipelines, heavy ETL processing, and parallel data analytics.
